title: From Vibes to Production: Evaluating and Shipping AI Agents That Work 201 — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
talk_summary: Laurie Voss argues agents are nondeterministic, so traces rather than code are the source of truth; he demos adding OpenInference tracing, using a coding agent with skills to inspect traces, turning failures into evals, and a scheduled Signal agent that clusters failures into issues/PRs. The actionable core is a trace→eval→signal→fix loop, though the product pitch and auto-PR claims need skepticism.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument every LLM call, tool call, and agent turn as nested traces with inputs, outputs, cost, latency, and status metadata so debugging is based on actual runs rather than code inspection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every LLM call, every tool call, every agent turn, all of those things become a trace.

takeaways.what_they_do: Give coding agents installed skills/CLI access to pull traces and programmatically summarize span kinds, statuses, errors, and quality issues instead of humans reading traces one by one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The skills are what are giving it all the information here.

takeaways.what_they_do: Turn a bad trace or eval failure into a dataset item and evaluator, then keep regression evals so changes do not break previously good behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a production system should have a set of regression evals

takeaways.what_they_do: A scheduled agent reads eval failures/traces, groups similar failures, and creates a GitHub issue or draft PR with the trace link and suggested fix.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Inside those thousand there's a hundred that are the same failure. That is what we're going to go and fix.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the same trace/eval loop on the auto-fix agent: trace its work and use LLM judges to score whether generated PRs are good.
takeaways.evidence_quote: powerful LLM judges looking at the results of Signal

takeaways.what_they_do: Run trace/eval analysis periodically rather than continuously, with configurable cadence, so the expensive reasoning is batched.
takeaways.evidence_quote: runs every six hours by default, but that's configurable
